brief: One drawer and one spike, both at the very same corner of the same cell, touching.

requirements.requirement: One drawer and one spike, both at the very same corner of the same cell, touching
requirements.evidence: Configurator refused this directly: addDrawer at {q:1,r:0,level:0} key 's' (the cut face of piece:1,0,0;half-n, whose corner is the triple junction 0,0|0,1|1,0) returned SPIKE_CLASH — 'spike:0#0,0|0,1|1,0 stands at a corner this drawer fills', details.steps removes the spike before fitting the drawer, alternatives: []. The spike at that junction is the only spike geometry available (all three surrounding cells 0,0 / 1,0 / 0,1 meet only there), and the drawer on that half base fills that same corner, so the two cannot coexist touching at that corner. No drawer was placed; the build keeps the spike at the junction but no drawer, which is not the touching pair asked for.

check_build ran: meshClash 'clear', no rule errors (only LOOSE_BODY / OPEN_CAP_FACE house-style warnings on the leftover demonstration bases). House rules capOpenFaces/lockJoints and props were not applied, since no build meeting the brief exists to settle, cap or dress.

finish.summary: Not built as asked: a drawer and a spike at the very same corner of the same cell cannot coexist in Hex Cluster. I set up the exact geometry — three bases (0,0 full, 1,0 half-n, 0,1 full) meeting at one junction, spike placed at that junction (spike:0#0,0|0,1|1,0), then the drawer on the half base whose corner is that junction — and the configurator refused it with SPIKE_CLASH: the spike 'stands at a corner this drawer fills', offering only to remove the spike first, with no alternatives. The drawer physically fills the corner the spike occupies, so touching at the same corner is impossible; placing either one excludes the other. I left the demonstration bases and spike in place (no drawer), which does not meet the brief. A feasible alternative would be a drawer and spike at different corners/cells, or the spike on a different junction adjacent to a drawer cell.

events.text: Drawer + spike at the same corner — I'll check the current build and what fits where.

result.note: A drawer sits on the cut face of a half base: place a half base first. Half-n and half-s take any drawer style; half-e and half-w take a slide, swing or long drawer (find_sockets offers those once the half base is on). No place on the build takes this part right now. Change the build so it can (for example add the cells it needs beside or below it), then ask again. Guessing raw ops for a part with no offers rarely works.

A spike stands where three bases meet at a corner: place three bases around one junction first. No place on the build takes this part right now. Change the build so it can (for example add the cells it needs beside or below it), then ask again. Guessing raw ops for a part with no offers rarely works.
